headline: Medium-risk pair: shared filesystem and browser-capable ctx can leak or mis-handle outputs, while the course profile adds no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can run browsers and observes Claude Code events, so it may ingest untrusted content from browser/file outputs; the zoomcamp profile is a course artifact with no isolation or provenance controls. A shared filesystem or manual bridge is plausible, but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF ctx reads browser-rendered or file content as instructions
IF the pair shares a filesystem or copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from file/browser content
Separate workspaces for the two agents
Use a provenance tag on imported text
Review any copied snippets before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, while the zoomcamp profile exposes no explicit data-handling limits. Because the pairwise workspace and sharing model are undocumented, leakage is plausible but not proven; the safest rubric choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace or mount
IF ctx logs or indexes files containing sensitive material
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Remove sensitive files from shared paths
Rotate or redact runtime logs
Restrict MCP server access to least privilege
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write to filesystem and install packages, while the zoomcamp profile is runnable=false and shows no write surfaces. Direct conflict is not documented, but if both are placed over the same mutable workspace, package or file changes can collide; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable directory
IF an operator runs package installs or file edits through ctx while the other process reads the same tree
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Snapshot the workspace before changes
Pause one agent during package installation
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a harness/knowledge-graph style agent that can observe tool events, so its outputs may be treated as structured context by downstream systems; the zoomcamp profile has no verification step or evaluator role documented. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF downstream automation consumes ctx-produced summaries as authoritative
IF the zoomcamp side renders or acts on those summaries without verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on outputs
Add a verification checklist for downstream consumers
Mark generated facts as untrusted by default
Compare outputs against source files before use
requires-engineering: add provenance and validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, which can create retention or residency issues, while the zoomcamp profile is a public course with no sensitive-data handling claims. Only ctx is relevant here because the compliance risk is about its logging surface; the other profile adds no conflicting policy.
conditions: IF ctx logs contain regulated or personal data
IF those logs are retained beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Redact logs before storage
Set short log-retention windows
Avoid placing regulated data in ctx sessions
Review exported audit records
requires-engineering: implement retention controls
